A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of Mendelian randomization studies (Obesity Reviews, doi:10.1111/obr.70156) reported evidence that general adiposity is causally associated with depression [2].

passages.text:
[Evidence on the bidirectional association between obesity and depression > Obesity and depression are linked in both directions]
- A meta-review of systematic reviews found a statistically significant association between obesity and depression in all nine included meta-analyses, with odds ratios from 1.18 to 1.57 (BJPsych Open). - The association appears reciprocal and may be modified by age and sex. A 2010 meta-analysis of over 58,000 participants established a bidirectional association among adults aged 20 to 59; the association was not statistically significant under age 20 (as summarized by Friedman et al., Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2025). - Proposed mechanisms include HPA-axis (stress hormone) dysregulation, inflammation, weight stigma, body image, sleep and activity changes. - A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of Mendelian randomization studies (Obesity Reviews, doi:10.1111/obr.70156) reported evidence that general adiposity is causally associated with depression.

passages.text:
[Obesity in adults - Canadian clinical practice guideline (Wharton et al., CMAJ 2020) > Canadian adult obesity guideline - summary]
- Obesity is defined as a complex, progressive and relapsing chronic disease in which abnormal or excess body fat impairs health. - The guideline shifts the focus of obesity management toward improving patient-centred health outcomes rather than weight loss alone. - Clinicians are asked to move beyond simplistic "eat less, move more" messaging and address root drivers of obesity, while validating patients' lived experience. - It contains 80 key recommendations across 19 chapters, bookended by chapters on weight bias and on the care of Indigenous peoples. - BMI alone is not an accurate tool for identifying adiposity-related complications; combining BMI with waist circumference and clinical assessment is preferred. [Overweight and obesity are rising in Canada (Canadian Health Measures Survey 2022-2024) > Measured obesity in Canadian adults > Measurement caveats]
- Self-reported BMI tends to be underestimated compared with direct measurement, so survey estimates based on self-report are lower than CHMS measured estimates. - Waist circumference can reveal weight-related health risk not reflected by BMI; abdominal obesity thresholds follow Health Canada guidelines.

result.answer:
A meta-review of systematic reviews found a statistically significant association between obesity and depression in all nine included meta-analyses, with odds ratios from 1.18 to 1.57 (BJPsych Open) [2]. A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of Mendelian randomization studies (Obesity Reviews, doi:10.1111/obr.70156) reported evidence that general adiposity is causally associated with depression [2]. Recommendations should be health-focused and non-stigmatizing, in line with Obesity Canada guidance [1].

**Sources**
[1] Evidence on the bidirectional association between obesity and depression - Compiled summary of peer-reviewed literature (BJPsych Open meta-review; Frontiers in Psychiatry 2025; Obesity Reviews 2026) (2026-05-01). https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bjpsych-open/article/association-between-obesity-and-depression-in-adults-a-metareview/68BB5A02ED0A342F2BB518421D6BE0D1
[2] Evidence on the bidirectional association between obesity and depression - Compiled summary of peer-reviewed literature (BJPsych Open meta-review; Frontiers in Psychiatry 2025; Obesity Reviews 2026) (2026-05-01). https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bjpsych-open/article/association-between-obesity-and-depression-in-adults-a-metareview/68BB5A02ED0A342F2BB518421D6BE0D1

**Where to get support**
- Most provinces: dial 8-1-1 to talk to a registered nurse (tell me your province for the exact service).
- Community counselling: find your local Canadian Mental Health Association branch - https://cmha.ca/find-your-cmha/
- No family doctor? Walk-in clinics, pharmacists and 8-1-1 can help you start; ask about publicly funded counselling.
- Canada's Food Guide - https://food-guide.canada.ca ; a registered dietitian can personalise advice.
- Obesity Canada (patient resources, weight-bias-free care) - https://obesitycanada.ca
